These four Retain mapping rows keep distinct target IDs but their original endpoint pair is absent under the mapped cable ID in the current cable source. A route elsewhere is not treated as equivalent; review or restore the exact route identity.

originalAttributes.name: Marea Carey
originalAttributes.blurb: Hits the high notes across the Atlantic. Huge capacity, cheap waves.

originalAttributes.name: Grace Hopscotch
originalAttributes.blurb: Hops from New York to the UK and Spain.

originalAttributes.name: Dunno-ant
originalAttributes.blurb: Nobody remembers who it is named after.

originalAttributes.name: Ami-Tea
originalAttributes.blurb: A friendly cable with French manners.

originalAttributes.name: Hibernia Express-o
originalAttributes.blurb: The straightest line across the Atlantic. Traders pay double to save a few milliseconds.

originalAttributes.name: TAT-14 Retirement Home
originalAttributes.blurb: Laid last century. Cuts often, costs more, still somehow running.

originalAttributes.name: EllaLink-ing
originalAttributes.blurb: Brazil straight to Iberia, skipping the US entirely.

originalAttributes.name: SACS-y Cable
originalAttributes.blurb: South Atlantic, cool and confident.

originalAttributes.name: Columbus III-and-a-half
originalAttributes.blurb: Discovered the Atlantic again. Old, pricey and fragile.

originalAttributes.name: 2Africa-n-Back
originalAttributes.blurb: All the way around Africa and back. Cheapest capacity on the map.

originalAttributes.name: Equi-yes
originalAttributes.blurb: Always agrees with you. Iberia to West Africa.

originalAttributes.name: SEE-ME-WAVE 6
originalAttributes.blurb: Sixth in a long-running series. Europe to India to Singapore.

originalAttributes.name: PEACE-out
originalAttributes.blurb: Marseille to Singapore, then it leaves the party.

originalAttributes.name: AAAAAE-1
originalAttributes.blurb: Asia, Africa, Europe, and one more thing.

originalAttributes.name: A Pretty Gateway
originalAttributes.blurb: The pretty way around East Asia.

originalAttributes.name: Jupiterrible
originalAttributes.blurb: Named after a planet, behaves like one: big and far away.

originalAttributes.name: FASTEST
originalAttributes.blurb: Its predecessor was FASTER. Marketing had a good day.

originalAttributes.name: Crosspatch Pacific
originalAttributes.blurb: Crosses the Pacific, mildly annoyed about it.

originalAttributes.name: Pacific Lite
originalAttributes.blurb: Lighter on paperwork than its namesake. Still heavy on paperwork.

originalAttributes.name: Southern Cross-ed Fingers
originalAttributes.blurb: Old Pacific workhorse. Everyone hopes it holds.

originalAttributes.name: Hawaiki-wiki
originalAttributes.blurb: Quick Pacific crossing with a stop for snacks.

originalAttributes.name: Indi-Go-Down
originalAttributes.blurb: Singapore to Sydney via Perth, on the days it is up.

originalAttributes.name: Guam-bling
originalAttributes.blurb: A bet on a tiny island in the middle of the Pacific.

originalAttributes.name: Sushi Train Cable
originalAttributes.blurb: Sydney to Tokyo by way of Guam, going round and round since 2001.

originalAttributes.name: Aloha Mate
originalAttributes.blurb: Sydney to Honolulu, and not a metre further. Getting to the mainland is your problem.

originalAttributes.name: Cut Lunch Cable
originalAttributes.blurb: Perth to Singapore and Jakarta. Packed fresh every morning, and cut more often than a sandwich.

originalAttributes.name: Ferry Express
originalAttributes.blurb: Crosses Bass Strait faster than the ferry, and gets seasick less often.

originalAttributes.name: SMAP (Somewhere, Maybe Also Perth)
originalAttributes.blurb: Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide and Perth by sea, so your packets never have to cross the Nullarbor. Another one from the bloke who starts a fibre company every time he finishes a flat white.

originalAttributes.name: Oh-Man Australia Cable
originalAttributes.blurb: Perth to the Gulf across the Indian Ocean. Oh man, it is long.

originalAttributes.name: Cook Strait Talking
originalAttributes.blurb: Down the west coast and across Cook Strait to the Mainland. The ferries bounce about; the cable mostly doesn’t.

originalAttributes.name: Lord of the Tasman Rings
originalAttributes.blurb: One ring to bind Invercargill to Sydney, Melbourne and Auckland. It lands next to a paddock where someone is building an AI factory, which is how you know it might really happen.

originalAttributes.name: Tasman Global Excess
originalAttributes.blurb: Sydney to Auckland with plenty to spare.

originalAttributes.name: Bi-Frosted
originalAttributes.blurb: A rainbow bridge from Singapore to California, via Jakarta and Manila.

originalAttributes.name: Sushi-Jollibee Cable
originalAttributes.blurb: Southeast Asia to Japan, with snacks.

originalAttributes.name: Far-Ice-1
originalAttributes.blurb: Iceland’s lifeline to Scotland. Lonely but determined.

originalAttributes.name: Dance-Ice
originalAttributes.blurb: Iceland to Denmark, choreographed.

originalAttributes.name: Greenland Connect-the-Dots
originalAttributes.blurb: Hops via Greenland. Polar bears included.

originalAttributes.name: IRIS Scan
originalAttributes.blurb: Iceland to Ireland, brand new and still smells like plastic.

originalAttributes.name: AEConnect-the-Dots
originalAttributes.blurb: New York to Ireland: the tech-tax express.

originalAttributes.name: Havfun
originalAttributes.blurb: Danish for “sea fun”. Probably.

originalAttributes.name: Celtix Connected
originalAttributes.blurb: Dublin to London across the Irish Sea.

originalAttributes.name: Falcon Punch
originalAttributes.blurb: Dubai to Mumbai. Hits hard.

originalAttributes.name: Eye-Gee
originalAttributes.blurb: A gateway from Europe to India, through the Red Sea. Pronounced like a very surprised cable.

originalAttributes.name: C-Lion King
originalAttributes.blurb: Helsinki to Germany under the Baltic. Anchors keep finding it.

originalAttributes.name: Ulysseless
originalAttributes.blurb: Short hop across the North Sea. An odyssey it is not.

originalAttributes.name: Channel Hopper
originalAttributes.blurb: London to Paris under the Channel. Cheaper than the train.

originalAttributes.name: Med-Nauti-lust
originalAttributes.blurb: Across the Mediterranean, Egypt to France. Romantic, in a cable way.

originalAttributes.name: EASSy Peasy
originalAttributes.blurb: East Africa up to Europe via the Red Sea. Lemon squeezy.

originalAttributes.name: TEAMS-work
originalAttributes.blurb: Kenya to the Gulf. Makes the dream work.

originalAttributes.name: Mo-Net-y
originalAttributes.blurb: Brazil to Florida. The invoice arrives just as fast.

originalAttributes.name: Sea-Bras
originalAttributes.blurb: Straight from São Paulo to New York, skipping the Miami hairpin.

originalAttributes.name: SAM-1-and-Done
originalAttributes.blurb: An old ring around the whole continent, the long way round Cape Horn.

originalAttributes.name: Curie-osity
originalAttributes.blurb: Los Angeles to Chile, with a small detour for Panama.

originalAttributes.name: Caribbean Cruise Control
originalAttributes.blurb: Hops the Caribbean so Bogotá can skip the jungle.

originalAttributes.name: Tannat Wine Line
originalAttributes.blurb: Named after a wine. São Paulo to Buenos Aires, past Uruguay.

originalAttributes.name: Humboldt Penguin
originalAttributes.blurb: The first cable from South America to Oceania. 14,000 km of very lonely glass.

originalAttributes.name: WACS-a-Mole
originalAttributes.blurb: Up the west coast of Africa. Something on it is always down.

originalAttributes.name: SAFE-ty Not Guaranteed
originalAttributes.blurb: An old cable from Cape Town round to India, via some very small islands.

originalAttributes.name: Bay of Bengal Gate-Delay
originalAttributes.blurb: Fujairah to Mumbai, round the tip of India to Chennai, then on to Singapore.

originalAttributes.name: Eye-to-Eye
originalAttributes.blurb: Chennai to Singapore, looking it straight in the eye.

originalAttributes.name: Strait Outta Taipei
originalAttributes.blurb: A short cable across a very tense strait.

originalAttributes.name: Gulf Bridge Over Troubled Water
originalAttributes.blurb: Leaves the Gulf from Fujairah and runs up the Red Sea to Europe.

originalAttributes.name: AAG-ony
originalAttributes.blurb: An Asia–America gateway cable that breaks so often it has its own support group.

originalAttributes.name: Darwin Award Cable
originalAttributes.blurb: Darwin to Singapore via Jakarta. Survival of the fittest packets.

originalAttributes.name: J-G’day-A (Japan–Guam–Aussie)
originalAttributes.blurb: Brisbane to Tokyo with a beach break in Guam.

originalAttributes.name: SEE-ME-WAVE 4
originalAttributes.blurb: The previous generation. Still carries most of Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, held together with hope.

originalAttributes.name: Baltic Anchor Magnet
originalAttributes.blurb: Short hops under the Baltic Sea. Every passing ship seems to find it.

originalAttributes.name: Black Sea Shanty
originalAttributes.blurb: Istanbul to Bucharest's coast across the Black Sea.

originalAttributes.name: Concerto in Sea Minor
originalAttributes.blurb: North Sea workhorse from London to Amsterdam. Dark fiber pairs for sale by the dozen.

originalAttributes.name: Circe du Soleil
originalAttributes.blurb: Another London–Amsterdam route. Everyone has one, so prices are low.

originalAttributes.name: North Sea Shuttle
originalAttributes.blurb: Brand new, cheap, and it lands right next to your racks.

originalAttributes.name: I-ME-WE-Us
originalAttributes.blurb: India, the Middle East and Western Europe, all on one cable. Lands in Cairo on the way.

originalAttributes.name: Jeddah-i Express
originalAttributes.blurb: New cables increasingly land in Jeddah instead of Egypt. This one heads for India and Singapore.

originalAttributes.name: Red Sea Shortcut
originalAttributes.blurb: A quick hop across the Red Sea between Egypt and Saudi Arabia.

originalAttributes.name: Doha Detour
originalAttributes.blurb: Connects Doha to the rest of the Gulf, by sea, which is handy when the land border is closed.

originalAttributes.name: NO-UK-Way
originalAttributes.blurb: Norway to the UK across the North Sea. Fiber pairs for sale, because the oil money wanted a hobby.

originalAttributes.name: Celtic Norsemen
originalAttributes.blurb: Ireland to Norway, the long way round the top of Scotland. Vikings, but in reverse.

originalAttributes.name: Havhingsten Hoofbeat
originalAttributes.blurb: The Sea Stallion: Blackpool to Denmark, galloping round the north of Scotland.

originalAttributes.name: Shefa Sheep Line
originalAttributes.blurb: Scotland to Iceland via Shetland and the Faroes. More sheep than packets.

originalAttributes.name: Apollo 13 (Houston, We Have Latency)
originalAttributes.blurb: New York to the cliffs of Bude. It made it home in the end.

originalAttributes.name: Yellow Brick Road
originalAttributes.blurb: Long Island to Cornwall. Follow it all the way to the wizard in the cable hut.

originalAttributes.name: ACE of Spades
originalAttributes.blurb: Africa Coast to Europe: twenty-odd countries on one cable, from France to Cape Town. The best card in a lot of hands.

originalAttributes.name: SAT-3-Legged Stool
originalAttributes.blurb: West Africa’s first big cable, from Portugal to Cape Town. Old and wobbly, but still holding things up.

originalAttributes.name: MainOne-Track Mind
originalAttributes.blurb: Portugal to Lagos, with stops in Dakar, Abidjan and Accra. Only ever thinks about West Africa.

originalAttributes.name: Mint Tea West Africa
originalAttributes.blurb: Casablanca down the coast to Abidjan, served sweet and very hot.

originalAttributes.name: Set SAIL
originalAttributes.blurb: Straight across the South Atlantic from Fortaleza to Cameroon. No stops, no islands, no excuses.

originalAttributes.name: Sea-Comedy Hour
originalAttributes.blurb: The cable that brought East Africa online, from Durban up to Djibouti and on to Mumbai. Still tells the story at every party.

originalAttributes.name: Dare-Devil-1
originalAttributes.blurb: Djibouti down to Durban, hugging the East African coast. Laughs at pirates and anchors.

originalAttributes.name: Glo-in-the-Dark
originalAttributes.blurb: Cornwall to Lagos down the West African coast. Glows faintly when it is working.

originalAttributes.name: Pas de Câble
originalAttributes.blurb: Another hop across the Channel, with dark fiber for sale. There is always room for one more.

originalAttributes.name: Oil Rig Wi-Fi
originalAttributes.blurb: Stavanger to the Netherlands and England via every oil platform in the North Sea. The roughnecks stream a lot of football.

originalAttributes.name: Medusa Stare
originalAttributes.blurb: Lisbon to Barcelona and Marseille along the coast. Look straight at the latency graph and it turns to stone.

originalAttributes.name: Nuvem-ber Rain
originalAttributes.blurb: Portugal to the US Southeast via Bermuda. Means cloud in Portuguese, and is owned by one.

originalAttributes.name: Feeling Blue
originalAttributes.blurb: Genoa to Sicily and on to Athens, laid by a search giant that got tired of renting.

originalAttributes.name: Sicilian Spaghetti Junction
originalAttributes.blurb: Palermo to Marseille and Alexandria. Every Europe–Asia shortcut wants a stop in Sicily.

originalAttributes.name: Ouzo Express
originalAttributes.blurb: Athens to Alexandria, and up the Dardanelles to Istanbul. Opa!

originalAttributes.name: Boston Tea Party Line
originalAttributes.blurb: Boston to Dublin. Nobody has thrown it into the harbour yet.

originalAttributes.name: Clementine
originalAttributes.blurb: A small, sweet cable from Broadstairs to Ostend, then inland to Oostkamp. Not to be confused with any other citrus-flavoured cable.

originalAttributes.name: SEA-US Later
originalAttributes.blurb: Los Angeles to Hawaii, Guam and the Philippines. See you later, packets.

originalAttributes.name: Asia-America Gateaux
originalAttributes.blurb: California to Hong Kong via Hawaii and Guam. A layered cake of repairs.

originalAttributes.name: Echo-Chamber
originalAttributes.blurb: California to Singapore via Guam. Everyone on it agrees with each other.

originalAttributes.name: HANTRU-ly Yours
originalAttributes.blurb: Guam to the Marshall Islands, with a stop on every atoll that writes in.

originalAttributes.name: Coral Sea Shanty
originalAttributes.blurb: Sydney to Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands. Hums while it works.

originalAttributes.name: Gondwanna-Be
originalAttributes.blurb: Sydney to Nouméa. Wishes it were a supercontinent.

originalAttributes.name: Tonga Twister
originalAttributes.blurb: Fiji to Tonga, the only way in. Try saying it three times fast.

originalAttributes.name: Tui-Some-More
originalAttributes.blurb: Fiji to Samoa. Always room for one more packet.

originalAttributes.name: ASH-tray
originalAttributes.blurb: American Samoa to Hawaii and Samoa on old, smoky glass.

originalAttributes.name: Hono-tuna
originalAttributes.blurb: Tahiti to Hawaii, trolling for bandwidth.

originalAttributes.name: Mana-tea
originalAttributes.blurb: Samoa to Tahiti by way of the Cook Islands. Steeped slowly.

originalAttributes.name: Southern Cross-ed Fingers NEXT
originalAttributes.blurb: The old workhorse’s younger sibling: Los Angeles to Sydney with a branch to Fiji.

originalAttributes.name: Sol Survivor
originalAttributes.blurb: Florida to northern Spain via Bermuda and the Azores. It goes straight through the Triangle and has come out the other side every time. So far.

originalAttributes.name: Atlantis-2: The Sequel
originalAttributes.blurb: Argentina to Portugal via Brazil, Cape Verde, Dakar and the Canaries. Laid in 2000 and slowly sinking into legend.

originalAttributes.name: Canary in the Cable Mine
originalAttributes.blurb: Tenerife to the Spanish mainland. As long as it keeps singing, everything is fine.

originalAttributes.name: ARC-ade Ring
originalAttributes.blurb: A ring around the Caribbean from Florida to Central America, older than most of its customers.

originalAttributes.name: Americas-Too
originalAttributes.blurb: Florida to Brazil down the island chain, from the year 2000, and it shows.

originalAttributes.name: ECFS (Every Coconut Fully Spliced)
originalAttributes.blurb: Island-hops down the Lesser Antilles. Laid in 1995 and repaired after every hurricane since.

originalAttributes.name: Southern Cari-Bean
originalAttributes.blurb: Newer glass along the same island chain, from the phone company that sells to every island.

originalAttributes.name: ALBA-tross
originalAttributes.blurb: Cuba’s only cable, laid from Venezuela in 2011 and switched on two years later. Hangs around your neck.

originalAttributes.name: Columbus’ Fixer-1
originalAttributes.blurb: Florida to Jamaica and Colombia, discovering the same route a second time.

originalAttributes.name: Fibra-Linky
originalAttributes.blurb: A short cable from Jamaica to the Dominican Republic, the link nobody notices until it is cut.

originalAttributes.name: Conch-nected
originalAttributes.blurb: Nassau to Florida, the shortest hop to the mainland.

originalAttributes.name: AMX-1 Mexican Wave
originalAttributes.blurb: From Florida round the Caribbean to Brazil, the big phone company’s very own cable.

originalAttributes.name: LION-hearted
originalAttributes.blurb: Madagascar, Réunion and Mauritius tied together, with a second leg up to Kenya.

originalAttributes.name: METISS-ing Link
originalAttributes.blurb: The newest cable from South Africa to Madagascar, Réunion and Mauritius, shared by the islands’ own telcos.

originalAttributes.name: SEAS-shells
originalAttributes.blurb: The Seychelles’ first cable, to Tanzania, after years on satellite.

originalAttributes.name: A-CORN-y
originalAttributes.blurb: Anchorage to Oregon under the Gulf of Alaska, for when the other one breaks.

originalAttributes.name: Alaska United-We-Stand
originalAttributes.blurb: Alaska’s old cables to the Lower 48, with a branch up to Juneau.

originalAttributes.name: Aleu-Shun Fiber
originalAttributes.blurb: Kodiak to the Aleutians, switched on at the end of 2022. The crab boats were very excited.

originalAttributes.name: Quintillion Bits
originalAttributes.blurb: The first subsea fiber in the American Arctic: Nome to Utqiaġvik, then over the North Slope to Anchorage. Sea ice keeps repair ships away half the year.

originalAttributes.name: Top-Hat
originalAttributes.blurb: From Vancouver Island straight to Japan, the first new cable on Canada’s Pacific coast in decades.

originalAttributes.name: Connected Coast-er
originalAttributes.blurb: Fiber along British Columbia’s coast to towns that only had satellite.

originalAttributes.name: SKM (Salmon, Kamchatka, More salmon)
originalAttributes.blurb: Sakhalin to Kamchatka and Magadan, laid in 2016 so the peninsula could stop relying on satellites.

originalAttributes.name: RJCN (Rather Jolly Cable to Niigata)
originalAttributes.blurb: Nakhodka to Niigata across the Sea of Japan.

originalAttributes.name: Hokkaido Hop
originalAttributes.blurb: A short hop from Sakhalin to Hokkaido.

originalAttributes.name: Chukchi Chuckle Line
originalAttributes.blurb: Petropavlovsk to Anadyr, finished in 2022: Chukotka’s first cable, after decades of satellite.

originalAttributes.name: EC-Link-ed
originalAttributes.blurb: Curaçao to Trinidad along the coast of Venezuela.

originalAttributes.name: HAVSIL-ent Night
originalAttributes.blurb: Kristiansand to Jutland, a short, quiet hop across the Skagerrak.

originalAttributes.name: Skagen-Dazs
originalAttributes.blurb: From the Oslo fjord to the tip of Denmark, where two seas meet.

originalAttributes.name: Nor-Feast
originalAttributes.blurb: A buffet of landings down the Norwegian coast, from the oil fields to Oslo.

originalAttributes.name: E4-ward Thinking
originalAttributes.blurb: Germany to Bornholm and Copenhagen, then up the Swedish coast to Stockholm. Anchors permitting.

originalAttributes.name: Eastern Light-weight
originalAttributes.blurb: Stockholm to Helsinki across the archipelago. Light, quick and right where the ships drop anchor.

originalAttributes.name: Elisa-bet
originalAttributes.blurb: Helsinki to Tallinn, cut by passing anchors more than once.

originalAttributes.name: Ventspils Venting
originalAttributes.blurb: Latvia to Gotland and on to Stockholm. Cut in 2025, mended a month later.

originalAttributes.name: BCS (Baltic Cable Snapped)
originalAttributes.blurb: Lithuania to Gotland since 1997, and very popular with dragging anchors.

originalAttributes.name: SJC2: Electric Boogaloo
originalAttributes.blurb: The sequel: Singapore to Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan and Korea, lit in 2025.

originalAttributes.name: ADC (A Direct Cable, Mostly)
originalAttributes.blurb: Singapore, Thailand, Hong Kong, Manila and Japan, with as few detours as the South China Sea allows.

originalAttributes.name: ASE-y Does It
originalAttributes.blurb: Japan to Singapore by way of Manila and Hong Kong, no rush.

originalAttributes.name: APCN-2 Fast 2 Furious
originalAttributes.blurb: A ring round East Asia from 2001: Singapore, Hong Kong, Manila, Taipei, Shanghai, Seoul and Tokyo.

rows.originalName: EAC-C2C (Every Asian City, Coast to Coast)

originalAttributes.name: EAC-C2C (Every Asian City, Coast to Coast)
originalAttributes.blurb: Another ring round East Asia, this one from the telco that owned half of them.

originalAttributes.name: FLAG-pole Europe-Asia
originalAttributes.blurb: Cornwall to Japan the long way: through the Mediterranean, the Red Sea and every strait on the way. Since 1997.

originalAttributes.name: FLAG Loop-de-Loop
originalAttributes.blurb: Hong Kong, Taipei, Seoul and Tokyo in one loop.

originalAttributes.name: SEE-ME-WAVE 5
originalAttributes.blurb: Marseille to Singapore with a stop at every port on the way, Muscat and Colombo included.

originalAttributes.name: Unity-corn
originalAttributes.blurb: Tokyo to Los Angeles, built by a search engine and five telcos holding hands.

originalAttributes.name: Tata’s Got Network
originalAttributes.blurb: Singapore to Tokyo via Vietnam and Hong Kong.

originalAttributes.name: TPE (Totally Pacific Express)
originalAttributes.blurb: Seattle straight to Shanghai, Seoul and Taipei.

originalAttributes.name: Hong Kong–Guam Gong
originalAttributes.blurb: Hong Kong to Guam, where the Pacific cables all meet.

originalAttributes.name: MIST-ery Tour
originalAttributes.blurb: Mumbai and Chennai to Malaysia and Singapore, lit in 2025. Where exactly it lands is a bit of a mystery.

originalAttributes.name: IAX-cellent
originalAttributes.blurb: Mumbai to Singapore with a stop in the Maldives.

originalAttributes.name: TIC-Tac
originalAttributes.blurb: Chennai to Singapore in one short hop.

originalAttributes.name: TW1-light
originalAttributes.blurb: The Emirates, Oman and Pakistan on one light little cable.

originalAttributes.name: MCT (Malaysia, Cambodia, Tuk-tuks)
originalAttributes.blurb: Malaysia to Thailand round the Gulf of Thailand, with a stop in Cambodia.

originalAttributes.name: KJCN (Kimchi-Japan Cable Network)
originalAttributes.blurb: Busan to Kyushu, the shortest way between Korea and Japan.

limitations: No current file path is treated as evidence that its original behavior was retained.
Source-symbol checks report literal expression presence or root identifier presence only; they do not resolve JavaScript expressions.
Only cable system identity/name/price/age and cable-pair endpoint tuples are parsed as structured source literals in this audit.
Retained city, company, customer and gameplay behaviors require separate semantic tests; they are not cleared by this audit.
The source capture and latest upstream byte-hash comparison have different commit scopes and are reported separately.

The local upstream evidence contains the Git tree manifest with blob hashes, not a separate 352-file content archive; byte matches are recomputed from current working-tree files against that manifest.
